title: Find the thin-walled tube among three look-alike cylinders
instruction: Cylinders P, Q and R look the same and weigh the same. One is a thin-walled tube, one a thick-walled tube and one solid. Put the thin-walled tube in the red bin. The orange button opens and closes the start gate at the top of the ramp.
context: Telling parts apart by how they behave, when they look and weigh the same, is routine in quality inspection. With three cylinders and two lanes, one race cannot rank them: the robot has to plan a second comparison, or time runs in the same lane, and keep the starts fair.
setup: A wooden two-lane ramp (20 cm wide, 21.7 cm long, 15 deg, top edge 5.6 cm high) lies 25 to 45 cm in front of the arm bases, its top 35.5 cm to the left of the centre line between the arms and its foot 14.5 cm to the left, so cylinders roll toward the right arm. The two lanes run 30 and 40 cm in front of the bases (thin white lines), with an orange start gate across both lanes 7.5 cm below the ramp top. An orange push button (3.6 cm cap) opens and closes the gate; it stands 17 cm in front of the bases, 37 cm left of the centre line. A black finish line crosses both lanes 6.5 cm right of the centre line, and a 20 x 18 cm foam pad 17.5 to 35.5 cm right of the centre line stops the cylinders. Three grey cylinders P, Q, R (5 cm diameter, 6 cm long, 150 g, labels on the end caps, axes pointing away from the robot) rest in cradles of two low dark rails: P 20.5 cm out and 28.5 cm left of the centre line, Q 20.5 cm out and 16.5 cm left, R 12 cm out and 4.5 cm left. Two empty cradles sit 20.5 cm out, 1.5 cm left and 9.5 cm right of the centre line. A red bin (10 x 10 cm, 3 cm walls) stands 19 cm out, 19.5 cm right of the centre line.
scoring: 0: no cylinder or the gate button is touched. 0.25: a cylinder is touched or the gate button pressed. 0.5: at least one cylinder released through the gate rolls past the finish line. 0.75: the runs show the thin-walled tube slower than both other cylinders, directly or through a chain: in a race of two cylinders released together through the gate it crosses the finish line later, or, for runs in the same lane, its time from gate opening to the finish line is longer. 1.0: the 0.75 condition holds and only the thin-walled tube is in the red bin. The score is the highest level reached.
reset_notes: Hidden per trial (redrawn every trial from its seed): Which cylinder is which, a random permutation of I = 1.0, 0.7 and 0.5 m r^2. The ramp has two lanes, so one race ranks only two cylinders: the thin-walled tube must be shown slower than both others (e.g. a second race of the first race's loser against the third cylinder). A single race of P and Q misses the tube in 1/3 of episodes and never proves it. Timing a solo run of each cylinder in the same lane also works (the reference does this).
fidelity: Cylinder inertia is set directly (both bodies use the same collision rims). The foam pad is a velocity damper applied in code. The start gate is a kinematic bar. A cylinder resting behind the closed gate is squared to the lane in code (a start chute). The lane groove that keeps a racing cylinder straight is a soft lateral spring and yaw torque applied in code.
